channel.title: 100 Doors to Recursion
channel.description: One door a day for 100 days into the things I've made with AI, from my first app to the system I run now.

item.title: Day 8: The changelog that becomes content
item.description: changelog-digest: turn a day of changelog entries into a hook, a short story and video ideas. Something to try: Run the dry run on the sample changelog, then on your own.

item.title: Day 7: The perfection pass: ask for two critique passes before you look
item.description: pp2p and pp3p, two Claude Code skills: two or three critique passes, then a polish. Something to try: Before you read your agent's next piece of work, ask it for two critique passes that try to break it, then a polish.

item.title: Day 6: My Claude Code config, and the ramp: a 53-second first session in May, then 146 sessions from November 8 to December 11
item.description: claude-config-public: the operating-rules template. Something to try: Copy it to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and fill in the 5 placeholders.

item.title: Day 5: treehouse: a git worktree pool for running several coding agents side by side
item.description: treehouse, one bash file that needs only git: spin a worktree per agent, glance at which are dirty on one screen, and sweep only the clean, merged ones. Something to try: Run treehouse spin 3, then treehouse glance.

item.title: Day 4: FriendForm: a form friends fill out from a link
item.description: A blank intake form to copy into any form tool. Something to try: Take one questionnaire you send around as a document, rebuild it from these sections and cut every question you would not act on.

item.title: Day 3: My CRM, started on Replit from two pasted documents
item.description: dataguard: checks a SQL database for orphaned records and dates out of order (link goes up when it is ready). Something to try: Pick one table in a database you own and count the rows that point at a record that no longer exists.

item.title: Day 2: WebPerformanceToolkit: my first app in git, and its 33 hours of simulated scores
item.description: The first prompt template: twelve sections plus the real-data line. Something to try: Before your next build, fill in at least sections 1, 4, 5 and 6, then paste the whole thing as your first message.

item.title: Day 1: RobotTales: bedtime stories where robot siblings teach if/else, loops and variables
item.description: A bedtime-story prompt that teaches one coding idea. Something to try: Paste it into any chat model, fill in the three brackets, and read what comes back before you read it aloud.
